clue.text: That bread is mine thank you

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone claims a loaf as their own and politely thanks the giver.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for 'thank you'. 'That' and 'is' simply join the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, slightly leavened Middle Eastern loaf that opens into a pocket.

clue.text: Hifalutin young boy leads girl

indicators.note: leads says the boy's word comes in front of the girl's in the answer

parts.note: a lad is a young boy
Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A pretentious young lad walks ahead of his girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes affected, pretentious manners, the same idea as highfalutin pomposity.

clue.text: Sobriquet of a prison title

parts.note: the nick is British slang for prison
a title is what something is called, its name

explanation.surface: A jail is given an informal name, as if prisons had pet names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The nick' is everyday British slang for a prison or police station.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobriquet is an informal familiar name given to someone in place of their real one.

clue.text: An activist's nude dancing creates nervous disorder

indicators.note: dancing has the letters of the three words jigging about into a new order

parts.note: the S of the possessive counts as a letter of the fodder here

explanation.surface: A protester strips off and dances, causing a commotion of the nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges AN ACTIVISTS NUDE; the 's of 'activist's' supplies a needed S. The surface's 'dancing' also neatly fits the disorder's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Vitus' dance is an old name for Sydenham's chorea, a condition of involuntary jerky movements.

clue.text: Today in this place books disciples

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era, the years we are living in
in this place means here
NT is the New Testament, a set of books; NTS is the plural

explanation.surface: A reader says that today, here, they reserve some followers.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (anno domini) stands for the current era, hence 'today'; NT is the crossword abbreviation for the New Testament books.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherents are followers who stick to a leader or cause, as disciples follow a teacher.

clue.text: Of buccaneers from the racial pit

indicators.note: from signals the answer is made out of the letters of the following words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A phrase about something produced from a pit of race hatred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' tells you the answer is formed out of the rearranged letters of RACIAL and PIT; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Piratical is the adjective for pirates, and buccaneers were pirates of the Caribbean.

clue.text: Electrode terminal with a junction

parts.note: a node is a point where lines or branches meet

explanation.surface: A technical note describing a terminal joined to a junction in a circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The anode is the positive electrode, the terminal at which current enters a device.

clue.text: Robinia cultivated from place in Kenya

indicators.note: cultivated suggests the plant name has been worked over into something new

explanation.surface: A false-acacia tree is grown from stock taken out of East Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Robinia is the false acacia tree, which makes 'cultivated' read naturally as gardening; it actually rearranges the tree's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Frame carrying crate of beer, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is said out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: taken as the word spoken

explanation.surface: A frame for carrying a crate of beer bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crate' here is slang for a coffin, not a case of bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: A bier is the stand on which a coffin is carried at a funeral.

clue.text: He leaves the headless chicken to set

indicators.note: He leaves says the letters of he depart from the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: headless says the first letter of chicken is cut off

explanation.surface: A man walks away from a chicken running around without its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes HE out of THE, leaving T; 'headless' strips C from CHICKEN, leaving HICKEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauce or jelly that sets becomes firm, as one that thickens becomes stiffer.

clue.text: I'm having to stay in the same place reference

indicators.note: having means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: the letters of I'm without the apostrophe
to bide is to stay or wait

explanation.surface: Someone says they must remain in one spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm having' reads like possession but means the word I'm holds the other inside it; ibid is the familiar short form used in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem, Latin for in the same place, is the footnote abbreviation pointing back to a source just cited.

clue.text: A prisoner turns up at the festival

indicators.note: turns up in a down light says the letters read backwards

parts.note: a lag is a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: A convict appears at a fete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses the whole of A LAG. 'Old lag' is British slang for a long-serving prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive occasion or celebration.

clue.text: Forbidden content word of first ten

parts.note: a verb is a part of speech, a word

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word of

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that the contents of the first ten words are banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' joins the definition to the wordplay; 'first' picks only O from 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Verboten is German for not allowed, borrowed into English for anything prohibited.

clue.text: Awkward admiral to be just awkward

indicators.note: the second awkward says the letters are put together clumsily in a new order

explanation.surface: A naval commander is told to be clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'awkward' does two different jobs: the first defines, the second rearranges ADMIRAL TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit means clumsy or lacking skill, from French for badly handled.

clue.text: They are flag designers by the way

definitions.text: They are flag designers by the way

parts.words: They are flag designers by the way
parts.note: flag means a paving flagstone, and by the way means beside the road, so these are people who draw on paving slabs

explanation.surface: An aside mentioning some people who design national flags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner, but it is a flagstone; 'by the way' looks like an aside, but means at the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: Street artists who chalk pictures on paving stones for passing donations.

clue.text: Take out supplementary coat tails

parts.note: supplementary means extra, additional

indicators.note: tails here means the two ends of coat, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone removes an additional tailcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat tails' is a garment, but here gives the first and last letters of COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to pull it out or remove it.

clue.text: Rebuke again for soft fish

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A diner scolds a cook a second time over a limp fish.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for piano, quietly, in musical notation.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach someone is to express disapproval of them, a scolding.

clue.text: Pad up tam with hair

indicators.note: up says the word tam is read backwards

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A Scottish cap is padded out with a lock of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: A tam (tam-o'-shanter) is a Scottish woollen cap; 'up' turns TAM to MAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress is the thick padded base of a bed.

clue.text: Question paper of some complex amalgamation

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An exam paper made up of a complicated blend of questions.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a test set out on a printed sheet of questions.

clue.text: Varlet without royal buttons

explanation.surface: A servant who goes without the royal livery buttons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buttons' is the traditional nickname for a hotel or household page boy, from the rows of buttons on his uniform; 'without royal' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A varlet was a medieval attendant or young servant, and a uniformed boy servant is nicknamed buttons.

clue.text: Walk extremely eager having to spat

parts.note: a gait is a manner of walking

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of eager

explanation.surface: A keen walker who has fallen out with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spat' looks like a quarrel or the past of spit; it is the short cloth covering for the ankle.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a short covering worn over the shoe and ankle, a kind of short gaiter.

clue.text: Turkish military leader was, to a degree, a lizard

parts.note: an aga was an Ottoman commander or chief
MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: An Ottoman officer was, to some extent, a reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was, to' and 'a' are links; the surface's 'to a degree' sounds like 'somewhat' but supplies MA.
explanation.definitionFit: An agama is an Old World reptile with a large head, related to iguanas.

clue.text: Sound promotion facing American fleet

parts.note: a sound is a stretch of sea, an arm of the sea
ad, advertisement, is a promotion

explanation.surface: Sound advertising is placed beside an American one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like noise or healthy, but is a sea inlet, an arm of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, after the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Loving to fuss round

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother
a ring is round in shape

explanation.surface: A doting parent fusses around a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring means showing deep affection and devotion.

clue.text: Pool made by a cat?

explanation.surface: Whether a pool of water was made by a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: A kitty is both a shared fund of money and a pet name for a cat; the surface teases a puddle left by a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a pot of money pooled by a group, and also a childish word for a little cat.

clue.text: Heard I screams for cold treats

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: the phrase spoken out loud

explanation.surface: Someone yells in the first person in exchange for frozen desserts.
explanation.walkthrough: From the playground rhyme 'I scream, you scream, we all scream for ice cream'.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen sweet dairy desserts eaten as a treat.
